headline: ARY does not need a baby range built — it already lists 228 baby SKUs, 124 of which have NEVER been purchased once, every Huggies code and every Pampers monthly-pack code among them, and only SEVEN diaper units sit on the shop floor today; fix the size ladder, the reorder levels and one live IMS Act breach (four feeding bottles sold below MRP) and the category goes from Rs 3,327 to roughly Rs 30,000 a month of infant demand for Rs 45,000 one-off — break-even is 3-4 regular babies against an estimated 32, but the whole prize is 0.4% of ARY's gross profit, so run it as a two-week service fix and never as a growth project.

findings.claim: The brief's premise is wrong. ARY does not have three baby SKUs — it has 228 active baby SKUs across 13 subgroups. The 'three Baby Accessories SKUs' is one mis-named subgroup (ID 1031: Rikang Joyful Feeder, Baby Finger Brush, Camera Baby Soother), not the range. This changes the whole job from 'launch a category' to 'repair a broken one'.
findings.evidence: ary query: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(CASE WHEN IsActive=1...) FROM ProductMaster WHERE SubGroupID IN (SELECT SubGroupID FROM SubGroupMaster WHERE SubGroupName IN ('Baby Diaper','Milk Feeder','Baby Soap','Baby Cream','Baby Oil','Baby Lotion','Baby Shampoo','Baby Powder','Baby Accessories','Baby Poeder','Wipes','Cerelac','Lactogen')) → 228 skus / 228 active
findings.number: 228 SKUs, all active: 73 Baby Diaper, 35 Cerelac, 23 Wipes, 18 Milk Feeder, 17 Baby Soap, 15 Baby Cream, 15 Baby Oil, 11 Baby Lotion, 9 Lactogen, 7 Baby Shampoo, 3 Baby Powder, 3 Baby Accessories, 1 'Baby Poeder' typo
findings.soWhat: No new codes, no new suppliers, no approvals. Everything needed is already in FusionERP8 with costs and selling prices set. The plan is a two-week reorder-and-repricing job, not a quarter-long launch.

findings.claim: 124 of the 228 baby SKUs have never been purchased even once since the books opened on 2023-04-01. That includes ALL ELEVEN Huggies codes and ALL THREE Pampers monthly-pack codes — the exact packs a resident family would buy. The codes exist with landed costs and prices already keyed; nobody ever placed the order.
findings.evidence: ary query with CTE b AS (SELECT DISTINCT ProductID FROM PurchaseDetail): 228 baby SKUs, 124 never_purchased_ever. Per-SKU: 'Huggies Huggies Pants Large', 'Huggies Pants (S-2 Pants)', 'Huggies Active Baby 19 Pads Small', 'Pampers Monthly Pack 76 Pants', 'Pampers Monthly Pack Large 64 Pants', 'Pampers Monthly Pack Medium 38 Pants' all return qty_purchased=0 AND qty_sold=0. ProductChildMaster shows them fully priced: Monthly Pack Large 64 = cost 755.53, MRP 1049, ARY price 899.
findings.number: 124 of 228 never bought; 11 of 11 Huggies codes and 3 of 3 Pampers monthly packs at zero lifetime
findings.soWhat: This is a procurement failure with a paper trail, not a market that does not exist. The fix costs a purchase order, not a business case.

findings.claim: Only SEVEN diaper units are on the shop floor right now. The Ary Warehouse holds 152 units and Ary Pos — the counter customers actually walk into — holds 7 across four codes. 96% of the diaper stock is in the back store.
findings.evidence: ary query: SELECT p.ProductName, w.WarehouseName, s.Quantity FROM Stock s JOIN ProductMaster p JOIN SubGroupMaster sg WHERE sg.SubGroupName='Baby Diaper' AND s.Quantity<>0 → Ary Warehouse: Happy Skin S 40, M8 40, L7 40, S7 12, M6 12, L5 12 = 156; Ary Pos: S7 3, Happy Skin S 2, L5 1, L7 1 = 7
findings.number: 7 units on the counter vs 156 in the warehouse (4.3% floor-facing)
findings.soWhat: A mother who finds an empty peg once sets up an outside supply line and never comes back for any size. The single cheapest action in this whole report is moving stock 200 metres.

findings.claim: The size ladder is broken at both ends. No newborn diaper code exists at all in the 73, and only one XL code exists (Mamy Poko 6 Pants Xl, never reordered). Only S, M and L have ever sold. A baby's journey is NB→S→M→L→XL→XXL and ARY covers the middle three.
findings.evidence: ary query on SubGroupName='Baby Diaper' filtered LIKE '%XL%' OR '%NB%' OR '%New Born%' OR '%Newborn%' → 1 row (Mamy Poko 6 Pants Xl, ReorderInformation=false). 12-month size-band sales: 2-S 113 units/11 months, 3-M 162/13 months, 4-L 123/13 months; NB and XL bands return no rows.
findings.number: 0 newborn codes; 1 XL code, never reordered; 3 of 6 size bands ever sold
findings.soWhat: The leak mechanism is identified. Adding NB and XL/XXL is the difference between being a top-up shop and being the family's supplier.

findings.claim: Reorder discipline does not exist — and not just for baby care. Of 19,481 active SKUs across the entire store, exactly ONE has a reorder level set. On all 73 diaper codes: reorder flag off, reorder level 0, safety level 0.
findings.evidence: ary query: SELECT COUNT(*) skus, SUM(CASE WHEN ReorderLevel>0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM ProductMaster WHERE IsActive=1 → 19481 / 1. And on SubGroupName='Baby Diaper': 73 codes, reorder_flag_on=0, has_reorder_level=0, has_safety_level=0.
findings.number: 1 of 19,481 active SKUs has a reorder level; 0 of 73 diaper codes
findings.soWhat: FusionERP8 has the fields and nobody uses them. For most of the store that is untidy; for diapers, where one stockout permanently loses a household, it is the root cause. Setting 26 reorder levels is the highest-leverage hour in the plan.

findings.claim: A live IMS Act breach sits in ARY's own bills: four feeding-bottle SKUs were sold in the last 12 months BELOW the MRP printed on the same bill line. Feeding bottles are IMS-covered (s.2(c) includes the teat and valve) and s.4(c) read with s.2(j) and s.3(c) prohibits offering any inducement, discount or rebate to a buyer of them.
findings.evidence: ary query on SaleDetail 12m for SubGroupName='Milk Feeder': Speedex Milk Feeder Bottle Steel 140Ml MRP 479.00 sold at 350.00 (6 units, Rs 2,100); Small Wander Glass Feeder Bottle 125Ml MRP 225.00 at 191.25 (4 units); Small Wander Feeding Bottle 250Ml MRP 120.00 at 99.00 (3 units); Small Wander Milk Feeder 125Ml MRP 110.00 at 90.00 (1 unit). Source of the rule: IMS Act 1992 as amended 2003, s.4 text at https://www.bpni.org/docments/IMS-act.pdf; BPNI's own enforcement slide is precisely this fact pattern — 'Feeding bottle making company Medela was found selling its bottles on a discount... IMS Act section 4 does not allow any incentive like discounts to a buyer' (https://www.bpni.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/IMS-Act-complete-ppt-with-notes-12.10.2020.pdf). Penalty s.20(1): up to 3 years or Rs 5,000 or both.
findings.number: 14 bottles, Rs 3,252, discounted 15-27% below MRP; 9 of 18 feeder codes carry a below-MRP SellingPrice in ProductChildMaster
findings.soWhat: Rs 3,252 of revenue carrying a criminal-offence exposure, and the fix is a one-line repricing. Do this before anything else in the plan — it costs nothing and it recovers margin.

findings.claim: ARY is already compliant with the hardest-to-retrofit IMS provision. Section 10(1) bans volume-based remuneration or commission on IMS, feeding bottles and infant foods — and SPCommPercent is 0.00 on all 846 subgroups in the database, so no volume-linked pay exists anywhere.
findings.evidence: ary query: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(CASE WHEN SPCommPercent<>0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM SubGroupMaster → 846 / 0. Cross-checked per subgroup for all 14 baby subgroups: all 0.00. Rule: IMS Act s.10(1), verbatim text.
findings.number: 0 of 846 subgroups carry any sales commission
findings.soWhat: If ARY ever introduces a counter-staff incentive scheme, formula, infant food and feeding bottles must be carved out of it by name. Right now there is nothing to fix — protect that.

findings.claim: Infant formula is stone dead at Baru Sahib and should stay a two-SKU service item, never a display. Nine Lactogen codes are listed; ZERO sold in 12 months; only 6 packs were ever purchased in the store's whole life. It is also the lowest-margin line in the range.
findings.evidence: ary assort probe lactogen → 9 SKUs matched, 0 sold_12m, Rs 0.00. ProductChildMaster: Nestle Lactogen 1 400 Gm cost 361.99 / price 485.00 (ever_bought 3); Lactogen 1 200 Gm Tin cost 182.86 / 245.00 (ever_bought 3); Lactogen 3 400 Gm cost 244.84 / price 278.00 = 11.9% GM; all other 6 codes ever_bought 0.
findings.number: 9 codes, 0 sold in 12m, 6 packs ever bought, 11.9-25.4% GM
findings.soWhat: There is not one regular formula buyer in the township. Two codes at two packs each is a Rs 1,800 exposure to write-off and buys the goodwill of the one mother a year who needs it. Anything more is dead stock in a legally booby-trapped line.

findings.claim: ARY's Lactogen 1 400g price master says MRP 485 while the pack's actual 2026 market MRP is Rs 450-460. Either ARY holds an older/tin SKU or it is priced above MRP — a Legal Metrology exposure separate from the IMS Act.
findings.evidence: ARY ProductChildMaster: Nestle Lactogen 1 400 Gm, MRP 485.00, SellingPrice 485.00. External 2026: Rs 450 at BigBasket (https://www.bigbasket.com/pd/240180/) and Rs 450 at 1mg (https://www.1mg.com/otc/nestle-lactogen-pro-1-powder-infant-formula-up-to-6-months-with-probiotic-and-prebiotics-otc370713); Rs 460 MRP at Apollo (https://www.apollopharmacy.in/otc/lactogen-pro-1-400g-refill). Tin packs are dearer than bag-in-box, which may explain 485.
findings.number: ARY 485 vs market 450-460 (bag-in-box)
findings.soWhat: Check the physical pack before reordering. Selling above the printed MRP is an offence and this line has zero offtake to justify the risk.

findings.claim: Cerelac cannot be shelf-faced deeply, because the pack reaching Indian retail in Aug-2026 had only about three months of life left. ARY sells 13 packs a year against 35 listed codes — any facing deeper than two packs is a guaranteed write-off.
findings.evidence: PharmEasy listing for Nestle Cerelac Wheat Apple 300g bag-in-box, fetched 2026-08-28: MRP Rs 259.97, 'Expires on or after 26/11/2026' (https://pharmeasy.in/health-care/products/nestle-cerelac-baby-cereal-with-milk-wheat-apple-from-6-months-300g-bag-in-box-pack-32156). ARY side: ary assort probe cerelac → 34 codes, 6 sold, Rs 3,878 in 12m; 12-month unit count 13 packs; ProductChildMaster costs Rs 128-277 against prices Rs 172-345, GM 12.6-25.4%.
findings.number: ~3 months residual shelf life at point of retail supply; ARY offtake 13 packs/yr; Cerelac GM 17.9% realised (lowest of the 10 baby lines)
findings.soWhat: One facing, one flavour (Wheat-Apple 300g), two packs deep, reordered on sale. Deactivate the other 32 Cerelac codes so the buyer stops seeing a phantom range.

findings.claim: 72% of what looks like 'baby care' revenue is almost certainly not babies — it is 2,657 boarding students buying baby soap, shampoo, powder and lotion as their own personal care. Rs 20,851 of it was rung up at ARY CLOTHING, a garment counter.
findings.evidence: 12m by subgroup and warehouse: Ary Clothing sold Baby Shampoo Rs 6,886, Baby Powder Rs 6,755, Baby Soap Rs 5,684, Baby Oil Rs 3,757, Wipes Rs 2,749, Baby Cream Rs 1,290, Baby Lotion Rs 210. Named-customer check on all baby-item bills lifetime returns school students (Gurleen Kaur D/O Gurpreet Singh, Akshmeet Singh S/O Jaswinder Singh, Ananya Kumari D/O Nandan Kumar…), not staff families. Unambiguously-infant lines (diapers + feeders + Cerelac + Lactogen) = Rs 39,919 of the Rs 1,46,173 total.
findings.number: Rs 1,06,254 of Rs 1,46,173 (72.7%) is toiletries usable by anyone; Rs 39,919 (27.3%) is unambiguously infant
findings.soWhat: Do not size the baby plan off Rs 1.46 lakh. The infant number is Rs 39,919/yr = Rs 3,327/month. And the toiletry half needs re-filing as student personal care or the buyer will keep mis-reading demand as baby demand.

findings.claim: Every rupee of diaper revenue at ARY is Pampers, and the format is a 2-8 piece emergency strip. Eleven codes sold in 12 months, all Pampers, at Rs 25-105 a pack. MamyPoko stopped selling in 2024; Huggies has never been stocked.
findings.evidence: ary query on SubGroupName='Baby Diaper', 12m: Pampers M Size 8 Pants 79 units Rs 7,855; Pampers L Size 7 Pants 73 / Rs 7,224; Pampers Happy Skin Pants -S 62 / Rs 5,766; Pampers Pants M Size 2 Pants 36 / Rs 900; Pampers S Size 4 Pants 30 / Rs 1,380; then M6, M4, L5, S7, L4, L2. All 11 rows Pampers. MamyPoko last sale 2024-07-25 (M4) / 2024-05-23 (L4).
findings.number: 11 codes, 398 units, Rs 32,699, 324 bills, 100% Pampers, pack sizes 2/4/5/6/7/8 pieces
findings.soWhat: Pampers is the brand to build the ladder on — the shopper has already voted and the distributor line exists. Adding a second brand splits 398 units across twice the codes and guarantees more stockouts.

findings.claim: ARY's per-piece diaper pricing is already competitive with online India, so the leak is availability, not price. ARY realises about Rs 13.50 a piece; Huggies Wonder Pants M56 online works out to Rs 12.48 and M112 to Rs 12.65.
findings.evidence: ARY: Pampers M Size 8 Pants at Rs 99 = Rs 12.38/pc; L Size 7 at Rs 105 = Rs 15.00/pc; S Size 7 at Rs 100 = Rs 14.29/pc (SaleRate = MRP on every line, i.e. no discount). External Aug-2026: Huggies Wonder Pants M 56 Rs 699 and M 112 Rs 1,417 (https://pricee.com/diapers/huggies-diapers-products-price-in-india); Pampers Premium Rs 12/pc, MamyPoko Rs 9/pc, Huggies Rs 11/pc (babyjunctions.in 2026); Pampers All-Round S 7pc Rs 99, NB 17pc Rs 199 (https://www.pingmedoc.com/pharmacy/vs/pampers-vs-mamypoko-vs-huggies).
findings.number: ARY Rs 12.38-15.00/piece vs online Rs 9-12.65/piece
findings.soWhat: Do not discount to compete. Fix the ladder and the stock and the family buys at ARY because 30-50 km of hill road beats Rs 1 a nappy.

findings.claim: The monthly packs ARY has never stocked are the LOW-margin format. Its 8-piece strips run 22-36% gross margin; the Pampers Monthly Pack 64 runs 15.96% and the 76 runs 16.34%. Stocking the ladder deliberately trades margin for retention.
findings.evidence: ary query on ProductChildMaster for SubGroupName='Baby Diaper': Monthly Pack Large 64 Pants cost 755.53 / MRP 1049 / price 899 = 15.96%; Monthly Pack 76 Pants 719.51 / 999 / 860 = 16.34%; Pants M Size 56 N 646.64 / 999 / 850 = 23.92%; M Size 8 Pants cost 63.48-75.00 / price 99 = 22.4-36.1%; realised 12m diaper GM 30.8% against a store-wide 28.3%.
findings.number: Strips 30.8% realised GM vs monthly packs 16-24%
findings.soWhat: Say this out loud to whoever signs the order: the monthly pack is not a profit play, it is a defection-prevention play. Keep the strip as the volume item and the monthly pack as the one-per-size anchor.

findings.claim: Wipes, not diapers, are the profit engine of a baby range — and they are outside the IMS Act entirely, so they can be displayed, bundled and discounted freely. Realised 45.5% gross margin, ARY's second-biggest baby line, and its single best-selling baby SKU.
findings.evidence: 12m realised: Wipes Rs 28,318 sales, Rs 15,421 estimated COGS, 45.5% GM (weighted-average PurchaseCost from PurchaseDetail vs SaleRate). Price master GMs: Sea Bird 72N 61.7%, Small Wonder 80N 57.2%, Tulips 20N Caramel 53.8%, Tulips 72 44.6%, Savlon 72N 42.0%. Best-seller: Tulips Wet Wipes 25 Aloevera & Jasmine, 134 units in 12m at Rs 60, last sale 2026-08-19. Legal basis: wipes are not an infant milk substitute (s.2(g)), infant food (s.2(f)) or feeding bottle (s.2(c)).
findings.number: 45.5% GM vs 28.3% store-wide; 23 wipe codes, 10 sold, 13 never purchased
findings.soWhat: Lead the shelf with wipes. It is the only baby line where ARY can run a promotion without a legal opinion, and it carries the fattest margin in the store.

findings.claim: Eight lines a township of 5,000 needs have NO code at all — not dead codes, no codes. Diaper rash cream, nappy pads, baby laundry wash, teether, bib, gripe water, baby toothpaste and baby thermometer all return zero on a name search across every group.
findings.evidence: ary assort probe run for each term: 'diaper rash' → 0 SKUs, 'nappy' → 0, 'teether' → 0, 'bib' → 0, 'gripe' → 0, 'romper' → 0, 'onesie' → 0, 'mittens' → 0, 'walker' → 0, 'high chair' → 0. Available externally and cheap: Himalaya Diaper Rash Cream 20g Rs 84, Germ Free Baby Laundry Wash 1L Rs 425, Kids Orange Toothpaste 80g Rs 133 (https://himalayawellness.in/collections/baby-care, fetched 2026-08-28).
findings.number: 8 must-have lines with zero codes; Himalaya covers 3 of them at Rs 84-425
findings.soWhat: Diaper rash cream in particular: every diaper-buying household needs it, ARY sells 398 diaper packs a year and cannot sell the Rs 84 cream that goes with them. It is the highest-attach, lowest-risk addition on the list.

findings.claim: No new vendor is needed. ARY already buys baby stock from five named local wholesalers, three of them within the last three weeks, and the top two do Rs 87.5 lakh and Rs 58.2 lakh of total business with ARY.
findings.evidence: ary query joining PurchaseDetail/PurchaseHeader/AccountMaster on the 11 baby subgroups: Himachal Wholesale Syndicate Rs 1,25,069 of baby cost / 31 bills / last buy 2026-06-27 (Rs 87.5 L total, 94 bills); Nirman Associates Pvt Ltd Rs 68,314 / last 2026-08-11 (Rs 12.07 L total); Parhlad Chand Batra & Sons Rs 33,374 / last 2025-10-03 (Rs 58.2 L total, last overall buy 2026-08-14); Sita Ram Chaman Lal Rs 17,445 / last 2026-08-03; Baghat Enterprises Rs 17,320 / last 2026-07-06.
findings.number: 5 live suppliers; brands already on the ledger: Himalaya Rs 1.08 L, Johnsons Rs 75.9 k, Pampers Rs 75.8 k, Nestle Rs 27.0 k, MamyPoko Rs 9.7 k, Small Wander, Tulips, Babyhug, Cetaphil Rs 106
findings.soWhat: Kills the usual objection. The order can be placed this week on an existing account with an existing credit line.

findings.claim: Demand is remarkably steady, which is the signature of a resident base rather than pilgrims or visitors: 16-43 diaper bills every single month for 25 straight months, never zero, never a spike.
findings.number: 29 diaper bills and 41 packs a month, 25 months running, coefficient of variation ~30%
findings.soWhat: There is a real standing customer set — roughly 8-15 households buying strips repeatedly. That is the floor you are building on, and it is already above break-even.

findings.claim: The plausible under-2 population at Baru Sahib is about 32 children, from about 16 births a year among roughly 200 resident staff family quarters — but this is DERIVED, never counted, and it is the number every rupee in this plan scales off.
findings.evidence: Anchor: Eternal University's NAAC Self Study Report states 'more than 200 family accommodations for staff' plus a working women's hostel with '169 family accommodation' (captured in this workflow's population lane, /Users/damanpreetsingh/jivo-cli/ary-cli/assort/research/sweep/population.json, which also verifies EU 1,102 students and 145 faculty+admin from the EU 17th Annual Report). Derivation, no TFR needed: ~2 children per staff family over a ~25-year campus tenure = 0.08 births/household/year × 200 households = 16 births/yr; children 0-2 = 2 × 16 = 32; children 0-6 = 6 × 16 = 96, most of the 3-6s absorbed into Akal Academy pre-primary. Independent internal cross-check: feeding-bottle offtake 19 bottles in 12m and 130 lifetime over 3.4 years ≈ 38/yr, at 2-4 bottles per baby over two years ⇒ 10-19 new babies a year entering bottle use — the same order of magnitude.
findings.number: ~16 births/yr; ~32 children under 2; ~96 under 6 (range 20-45 under 2)
findings.soWhat: Every revenue figure below moves linearly with this. Two phone calls — Kalgidhar Trust HR for quarters and occupancy, Akal Charitable Hospital (100 beds, 43,706-47,848 OPD/yr) for annual deliveries — replace the estimate with a fact and could move the answer plus or minus 40%.

findings.claim: ARY currently captures about 6% of the resident baby wallet. Addressable is roughly Rs 1,870 per baby per month; ARY takes Rs 104.
findings.evidence: Basket built from verified 2026 prices: diapers 2/day × 30 × Rs 13.50 = Rs 810; wipes 1 × 72s at Rs 130; Himalaya bath/skin basket amortised Rs 264 (soap 75g Rs 45/mo, shampoo 100ml Rs 106 per 3mo, oil 100ml Rs 140 per 3mo, lotion 200ml Rs 115 per 2mo, powder 100g Rs 112 per 3mo, rash cream 20g Rs 84 per 2mo — all from himalayawellness.in Aug-2026); Cerelac 2 × Rs 275 × 75% of base = Rs 413; formula Rs 450 × 3 × 15% of base = Rs 203; bottle/soother amortised Rs 50. Total Rs 1,870. Captured: unambiguous infant lines Rs 39,919/yr ÷ 12 ÷ 32 babies = Rs 104/baby/month. Deliberately conservative against the external benchmark of Rs 5,000-6,000/month on diapers alone for an average Indian parent (https://www.ipfapp.in/blog/cost-of-raising-a-baby-in-india/) because hill-township families diaper part-time.
findings.number: Rs 1,870/baby/month addressable; Rs 104 captured = 5.6%
findings.soWhat: A range that is merely present should reach 50% capture in a township whose nearest market town is 30-50 km of hill road. That is the entire size of the prize.

findings.claim: Break-even is 3-4 babies buying regularly, and ARY already clears it. Ceiling is Rs 7,400/month of gross profit at 32 babies — 0.4% of ARY's gross profit — so this is a service fix, not a growth project.
findings.evidence: Incremental GM per baby/month = Rs 1,870 addressable × 50% capture × 28% blended GM = Rs 262. Fixed costs: one 4-ft bay plus IMS-compliant shelf card Rs 12,000 amortised over 36 months = Rs 333/month, plus worst-case Cerelac+formula expiry write-off Rs 6,000/yr = Rs 500/month. Break-even = (333+500)/262 = 3.2 babies. Central case 32 babies × Rs 262 = Rs 8,384 gross, net of write-off risk ≈ Rs 7,400/month = Rs 89,000/yr. Store gross profit for comparison: 12m matched sales Rs 7,46,49,891 less estimated COGS Rs 5,35,45,068 = Rs 2.11 Cr at 28.3% (ary query joining weighted-average PurchaseCost to 12m SaleDetail).
findings.number: Break-even 3-4 babies; Rs 3,300/mo GP at 16 babies, Rs 7,400 at 32, Rs 14,800 at 60; ceiling 0.42% of ARY's Rs 2.11 Cr gross profit
findings.soWhat: Approve it in a two-line note, give it to the counter in-charge, and do not put it on a strategy slide. The same two weeks spent on the dark Talwandi Sabo counter (Rs 3.35 lakh/month run-rate, 2,703 students) is worth 45 times more.

findings.claim: There is exactly one lawful discount in this whole category, and the Trust already owns the qualifying institution: s.5(a) permits distribution of infant milk substitutes, feeding bottles and infant foods to an orphanage, and s.8(5) lets an orphanage buy them below sale price.
findings.evidence: IMS Act s.5(a): 'no person shall donate or distribute infant milk substitutes or feeding bottles or infant foods to any other person except to an orphanage'. s.8(5): 'An orphanage may purchase infant milk substitutes or feeding bottles at a price lower than their sale price… such purchases shall not amount to an inducement'. Verbatim from https://www.bpni.org/docments/IMS-act.pdf. The Kalgidhar Society runs an orphanage at Baru Sahib alongside the old age home, charitable hospital and spiritual academy (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baru_Sahib).
findings.number: s.5(a) + s.8(5), one named exception
findings.soWhat: If the Trust's orphanage has infants, ARY can supply it at a concession lawfully — the only concessional infant-nutrition sale available to this business. Worth one email to establish whether the demand exists.

findings.claim: Nothing baby-food-branded may go inside Akal Charitable Hospital or any Trust clinic. Section 8(1) bans placards, posters and promotional material in a health care system, and s.2(d) defines that to include pharmacies and drug stores.
findings.evidence: IMS Act s.8(1) verbatim: 'No person shall use any health care system for the display of placards or posters relating to, or for the distribution of, materials for the purpose of promoting the use or sale of infant milk substitutes or feeding bottles or infant foods'. s.2(d) defines health care system to include 'a pharmacy, drug store'. BPNI notes authorised officers specifically 'check on the chemist shops for any special displays of baby foods'. ARY already bills Akal Hospital Baru Sahib (credit customer 00009, Rs 2,75,375 outstanding) and Akal De-Adiction Ward (001JH, Rs 11,32,890).
findings.number: s.8(1); ARY has 2 live health-facility accounts on the ledger
findings.soWhat: If ARY ever opens a counter in or beside the hospital — an obvious idea given 120-131 OPD patients a day — the infant-nutrition display is illegal there from day one. Design the counter knowing that.

findings.claim: Section 6 puts a stocking test on ARY, not just on Nestle: a pack whose label lacks the mandatory 'IMPORTANT NOTICE' block, or which carries a picture of a baby or a mother, may not be sold — and this is the ONE breach with a mandatory minimum prison term.
findings.evidence: s.6(1) requires 'important notice' in capitals plus (a) 'mother's milk is best for your baby' in capitals, (b) use only on a health worker's advice, (c) not the sole source of nourishment, (d) preparation instructions and a hazard warning, (e) ingredients, (f) composition, (g) storage, (h) batch/manufacture/use-by. s.6(2) bans pictures of an infant or a woman, saleability graphics, and the words 'humanised'/'maternalised'. s.11 requires the BIS Standard Mark on infant food and feeding-bottle containers. s.20(2): a s.6 or s.11(1) breach draws imprisonment of not less than six months, up to three years, and a fine of not less than Rs 2,000 — a floor, not a cap. Verified live on shelf: Apollo and 1mg both display 'IMPORTANT NOTICE: MOTHER'S MILK IS BEST FOR YOUR BABY' on Lactogen Pro 1 400g.
findings.number: s.20(2): minimum 6 months (reducible to 3 for special reasons) + minimum Rs 2,000
findings.soWhat: Give the goods-inward clerk a two-line check: notice block present, no baby or mother on the pack, BIS mark on the container. It takes five seconds and it is the only baby-care rule that can jail somebody.

findings.claim: Not one baby subgroup has any shelf space allotted. AreaAllotted is 0 for all 14 of them, so the range has never been given a physical home in the store.
findings.evidence: ary query: SELECT SubGroupID, SubGroupName, SPCommPercent, AreaAllotted, IsActive FROM SubGroupMaster for the 14 baby subgroups → AreaAllotted = 0 on every row (Baby Diaper 260, Milk Feeder 593, Wipes 846, Cerelac 349, Lactogen 550, Baby Soap 263, Baby Cream 257, Baby Oil 259, Baby Lotion 258, Baby Shampoo 1030, Baby Powder 262, Baby Poeder 261, Baby Accessories 1031, Food Supplement 462).
findings.number: 0 sq units allotted across 14 baby subgroups
findings.soWhat: Explains the seven units on the floor. Until a bay is assigned, replenishment has nowhere to replenish to.

findings.claim: The category is filed wrong in three places, which is why nobody reorders it coherently: feeding bottles sit under 'House Hold', a subgroup is spelled 'Baby Poeder', and the three genuine nursery accessories sit under 'Accessories' instead of with baby care.
findings.evidence: ary query on SubGroupMaster/ProductGroupMaster: Milk Feeder (593) → ProductGroupName 'House Hold'; 'Baby Poeder' (261) → Personal Care, 1 SKU, last sale 2024-12-15; Baby Accessories (1031) → 'Accessories', 3 SKUs, 0 sold ever. openQuestions: How many children under 2 and under 6 actually live at Baru Sahib? Everything here scales off ~32 under-2s that I derived from 'more than 200 family accommodations for staff' (Eternal University NAAC SSR) and a 25-year-tenure birth model. Kalgidhar Trust HR / Akal Academy administration can answer it in one call, and it could move the revenue plus or minus 40%.

How many deliveries a year does Akal Charitable Hospital Baru Sahib do, and does its maternity ward want an institutional supply account? It is already ARY credit customer 00009 (Rs 2,75,375 outstanding), 100 beds, 43,706-47,848 OPD a year. A hospital PO is the only way baby volume becomes material here, and it is compliant because it is not a display.

Does the Trust's Baru Sahib orphanage have infants? If yes, IMS Act s.5(a) and s.8(5) permit the only lawful below-price supply of formula and feeding bottles in this category. Nobody at ARY appears to have asked.

Why has ARY never once ordered a Pampers monthly pack or a single Huggies unit, when the codes have been fully priced in ProductChildMaster since the books opened? Is it a supplier minimum-order constraint, a working-capital rule, or simply that nobody looked? The ARY purchase in-charge and Himachal Wholesale Syndicate know; I only know the order was never placed.

Is ARY's Lactogen 1 400g at MRP 485 the tin (dearer) or the bag-in-box (verified market MRP Rs 450-460)? If it is the bag-in-box, ARY is priced above MRP — a Legal Metrology issue independent of the IMS Act. Needs someone to read the physical pack.

What is the manufacturer's stated shelf life on diapers and on unopened Lactogen? Both my source fetches 404'd. It only matters for how deep the monthly-pack facings can go, but do not quote 'diapers do not expire' as a fact until somebody reads a carton.

Do resident staff families already have an outside diaper supply line — an Amazon/Flipkart delivery to 173101, a monthly Solan or Nahan run, or gifts from family? That determines whether 50% capture is achievable or optimistic, and no data in FusionERP8 can see it. Twenty conversations at the counter would settle it.

Should the store-wide reorder-level void be a separate project? 1 of 19,481 active SKUs has a ReorderLevel set. Baby care is where it costs a customer permanently, but the same void almost certainly explains dead lines across Medicare (Rs 3.40 L on 272 SKUs), Frozen and Dairy too. That is a bigger prize than this lane.
confidenceGap: The baby headcount is ESTIMATED and never counted, and every revenue line scales linearly off it. I derived ~16 births/year and ~32 children under 2 from one verified anchor ('more than 200 family accommodations for staff' in Eternal University's NAAC Self Study Report) plus a tenure model, and cross-checked it against ARY's own feeding-bottle offtake (19 bottles in 12 months, 130 lifetime, implying 10-19 new babies a year) — two independent methods that agree on the order of magnitude but not the number. ARY's transaction data cannot narrow it because 97% of bills belong to the anonymous Cash customer 00001, and the campus is not a normal age pyramid (2,657 of ~4,500 residents are boarding students), so no census ratio applies. Critically, ARY's tiny diaper volume — about 2,357 pieces a year, roughly one baby's full-time use — is consistent with BOTH 'there are almost no babies' and 'there are 32 babies and ARY captures 6% of them because it has never stocked a month's supply in any size'. Those two readings differ by an order of magnitude in the upside and I cannot separate them from the database. What is NOT uncertain, and does not depend on the headcount at all: the 124 never-purchased codes, the 7 units on the counter, the missing newborn and XL sizes, the 1-of-19,481 reorder levels, and the four feeding bottles sold below MRP — all pulled live and all worth fixing on their own.
